newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Great Eagle to finalise HK$6 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Great Eagle to finalise HK$6 bln loan.

text.p: Great Eagle Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it expected to finalise with banks "within months" a loan of about HK$6 billion for the development of an office and commerical complex in Hong Kong's Mongkok district.

Deputy chairman and managing director Lo Ka-shui told reporters after an annual general meeting that premium for the site, in a busy commercial district in Kowloon, was still being negotiated with government.
He said the project, a profit-sharing joint venture with Land Development Corp, was not expected to contribute to group earnings until 2000 when its first phase was scheduled to be completed.
Assistant director Adrian Lee said the firm had already invested HK$3 billion in the project.
Lo said shelving the spinoff of Tai Shan Properties Ltd, about HK$700 million of whose proceeds had been intended for the Mongkok development, would not leave the project strapped for funds.
"It has no big effect on us because the sum intended to be raised (from Tai Shan) was not big," Lo said.
He added it was easy for the firm to borrow from banks for the project expected to be worth at least over HK$10 billion in value.
Loans for the project would bring the group's gearing to 50 percent from the present 22 percent if Great Eagle sold no part of the project, he said.
But the group would sell part of the development which would reduce the gearing to below 50 percent, and retain the rest for leasing, he said.
Lee said the group intended to start with selling 700,000 square feet of offices.
Lo said the company decided to shelve the spin-off of Tai Shan, its office and commercial property portfolio, in view of the unfavourable stock market conditions.
"The market is only so-so and there are concerns about an interest rate rise," he said.
In February, the group said it planned to spin off the unit to raise up to HK$2.50 billion.
Lo said he would not dismiss the possibility of the spin-off in the future, although not in short term. He did not elaborate.
The company was not thinking of spinning off the group's hotel operation at present, he said.
Great Eagle was interested in bidding for the development rights above the Kowloon station of the airport railway, he said.
